metadata.verifiedAgainst: Hindi reference summaries (HI Reference) rendered on the same page
metadata.dataset: MILDSum (10 samples), Qwen3.5-4B (Q4_K_M) zero-shot / few-shot / CoT EN->HI legal summarization
methodology: Extracted the full page data (10 x {hiReference, zeroShot, fewShot, cot}) from the Next.js RSC payload and cross-validated every text against the SSR-rendered HTML (exact match).
Extracted the highlight-span data (122 spans) and the error-annotation data (736 details + counts) from the site JS bundle (chunk d4189770b3d1bfae.js).

Automated checks: every highlight span was substring-tested against its target output text; every reference-omission span was substring-tested against the reference and each tagged output (whitespace-normalized).

Manual linguistic verification of every item against the Hindi reference text, by sample and method, including Hindi legal terminology, fabricated entities, dates, names, numbers and misattributed annotations.

Verdicts: confirmed / partially_confirmed / confirmed_with_rendering_bug (error real but the span never renders in the UI) / debunked / debunked_misattributed (claimed error belongs to a different method or does not exist in the texts or the reference).
notes: 21 of 122 highlight spans never render because their text does not exactly occur in the output (devanagari spelling variants, script-mixed Cyrillic/Latin text, or plain absence).

Several omission claims reference content (e.g. "BSNL v. Tata", "12 saal", "Roshan Lal", "Arundhati Katju", "Kinri Dhir", "SR Nazrul Ahmed") that does not exist in the Hindi reference at all, so they cannot be omissions relative to it.
A systematic zero-shot/few-shot misattribution pattern was found (e.g. Sample 1: "airtickar"/"bahaal"/"rasa"/"writ"/"karyakari adhikari"/Division Bench claims swapped between the two methods).
New errors are compared strictly against the Hindi reference text; some "fabricated" names/dates match the original English articles but are unsupported by the reference used for evaluation.
